items.title: Has Demna Solved Gucci's Identity Crisis?
items.summary: BoF critical review of the SS27 Store Show argues the collection reads as an urgent meditation on beauty and desire rather than a clear commercial answer, leaving open whether Demna's aesthetic can durably fix Gucci's identity and demand problem despite being called the hottest ticket of Milan week.

items.title: Gucci SS27, Demna trasforma la sfilata in boutique: la strategia di Kering
items.summary: Italian business-press analysis frames the store-set runway as Demna executing Kering's commercial mandate (entry-price Ophidia bags at 690 euros) while ironically mocking that same pressure. Notes Q2 2026 revenue of 1.41bn euros (-2% comparable) and questions whether success will be judged purely on the 'final budget figure' rather than creative merit, amid a wider shift of consumers toward fast fashion and secondhand.

items.title: From rappers to nonnas, Demna hits shuffle on Gucci stereotypes for SS27
items.summary: UK youth-culture outlet reviews the SS27 show as a survey of Gucci archetypes (tracksuited young rapper through to the classy Italian grandmother), reading it as playful and knowing rather than fully resolved, part of the broader post-show discourse questioning whether archetype-driven styling can rebuild desirability.

items.title: Forum Members Review the 'Vulgar' Gucci Spring 2027 Collection From Demna
items.summary: Fashion-forum thread aggregation shows overwhelmingly negative grassroots reaction to the SS27 show, with posters calling it 'a tragedy,' 'a pile of nothingness,' and predicting a flop; several questioned whether this could be Demna's final season at the house. Represents committed fashion-community sentiment, skewing harsher than most professional critic reviews.

items.title: Gucci S/S 2027 Milan discussion thread, page 2
items.summary: Ongoing fan-forum thread continues to run mostly negative the day after the show: posters call the womenswear 'abysmal, pretentious and bad overall' and one predicts 'another huge flop,' while a few say the menswear was more interesting though derivative ('Polo Ralph Lauren x Celine'). Multiple posters speculate about Demna's job security.

items.title: Milan Fashion Week: Gucci mise sur l'esthetique 'Boom Boom'
items.summary: French trade-press piece frames the SS27 collection as a deliberate rejection of quiet luxury via an exuberant, maximalist 'Boom Boom' aesthetic; notes that while Kering's sales decline continued after Demna's 2025 arrival, the pace of decline slowed in Q2, framing the show as a test of whether creative direction can support commercial stabilization.

items.title: Gucci Spring 2027 Ready-to-Wear Runway Review
items.summary: Trade-press runway review of the SS27 Store Show adds to the professional critical record on Demna's second collection, part of the broad and polarized wave of reviews published in the 48 hours after the Sept 25 show that split between qualified praise for ambition and skepticism about commercial translation.

items.title: Gucci.com Italian customer reviews - quality and repair complaints
items.summary: Aggregated Italian consumer-review pages show recurring complaints unrelated to the runway news cycle: shoes and belts failing within months (e.g., a 790-euro pair of Ace sneakers cracking after 3 months), costly paid repairs (130-200 euros) on items under a year old, and customer-service frustration describing Gucci's warranty as ineffective. Reflects a persistent quality-versus-price grievance among actual buyers, distinct from runway-driven brand sentiment.

items.title: Gucci second-hand sales increase while sales of new products decline
items.summary: Trade-blog analysis reports Gucci's resale volumes rising even as new-product sales fall, framing it as evidence of a demand mismatch: heritage archive pieces (Jackie, Marmont, Tom Ford-era items) retain desirability on resale platforms while current full-price collections struggle, a structural headwind for Demna's repositioning that the runway alone does not resolve.

items.title: Gucci's Demna blends aristocracy and pop culture at Milan Fashion Week
items.summary: Trade-press wrap describes the SS27 collection's mix of tartan-lined tailoring, cropped trousers, exposed-midriff suiting and 1980s Milanese references, presented in a mock-retail set intended to preview how Demna's aesthetic could reshape Gucci's physical stores.

items.source: X / TikTok (aggregated creator reaction, via secondary trade coverage)
items.title: Aggregated social reaction roundup to Demna's Gucci runway work
items.summary: Lifestyle-wire roundup compiles ongoing polarized social commentary around Demna's Gucci output, citing both harsh dismissals ('everything Demna does is one big cliche') and defenders praising his boldness, illustrating the sustained SNS-side split in public opinion beyond the professional critic tier.
